newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle post mostly higher closes.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle post mostly higher closes.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mostly higher after the April contract expired while feeder cattle finished higher but had slipped from new contract highs by the close.

Live cattle closed 0.025 cent per lb lower to 0.200 higher with only June off at 64.650 cents. April expired earlier at 69.925, up 0.600 cents, after trading as high as 70.100 cents on short covering.

Feeder cattle futures climbed to new contract highs in April through August and distant March before closing unchanged to 0.450 cent a lb higher with May up 0.200 at 72.400 cents. April set a high of 72.600 and May 72.700 cent.

Live cattle were influenced by the April contract until its expiration at 1200 CDT. But June failed to rally when April went off despite June's discount to cash. Expectations that cash cattle prices will slip seasonally into June curbed gains in that month but expectations of strong beef demand through May provided underlying support, traders said.
Prudential Securities bought June late while Cargill Investor Services spread long June/short August. Refco was a buyer of most back months early, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, funds bought August 68 calls and both bought and sold December 76 calls. Commercials bought June 68 calls and commission houses sold June 62 in 63 puts. Volatility was steady to weak in June and August, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures posted new contract highs on the early advance, boosted by rising cash feeder cattle prices, concern over cattle death losses in the upper Midwest and Plains states from storms and flooding and expectations of easing feed costs. But profit taking trimmed best levels late, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $72.16 per cwt, the highest level in over two years, since February 22, 1995.
Refco bought May late while Lind-Waldock sold, traders said. LIT division of First Options bought August while Refco sold, pit sources said.
